content: Glimepiride is an oral hypoglycemic medication that has been linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular mortality. It is essential to discuss with your healthcare provider the potential risks, benefits, and alternative treatments before starting this medication. Glimepiride is prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes, a condition where the body does not use insulin effectively, leading to elevated blood sugar levels. This medication works by stimulating the pancreas to produce more insulin and by increasing the body’s sensitivity to insulin. It can be used alone or in combination with insulin. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Glimepiride is available in tablet form and is typically taken once daily, preferably with breakfast or the first substantial meal of the day. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. Do not alter the dosage or frequency without consulting your doctor. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not discontinue it without medical advice. Before starting glimepiride, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease or diabetic ketoacidosis. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. If you become pregnant while taking glimepiride, contact your doctor right away. Additionally, if you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Follow all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet and discuss the safe consumption of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can lower blood sugar levels. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Glimepiride may cause fluctuations in blood sugar levels. Be aware of the symptoms of hypoglycemia (low blood sugar), which include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, irritability, mood changes, headache, numbness or tingling around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, and clumsy or jerky movements. Severe hypoglycemia can lead to confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness, requiring immediate medical attention. Hyperglycemia (high blood sugar) symptoms include extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, weakness, and blurred vision. If untreated, hyperglycemia can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis, a life-threatening condition characterized by dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, and decreased consciousness. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience these symptoms. Store glimepiride in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory for monitoring. Your doctor will order tests to evaluate your response to glimepiride and may instruct you on how to monitor your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. The brand name for glimepiride is Amaryl®.
